🔥 US S 5045 — Wildfires Could Now Trigger Air Quality Alerts

This bill updates the Clean Air Act to clarify how air quality monitoring data is handled when prescribed fires cause smoke.

It defines ‘exceptional events’ – events like prescribed fires – that could trigger air quality alerts.

The Administrator will revise regulations to reduce the burden on states to demonstrate an exceptional event, clarify the role of prescribed fires, and establish a process for reviewing state petitions regarding exceptional events.

The bill also creates a ‘Smoke Ready Communities’ program, offering competitive grants to states, tribes, and other entities to assess and mitigate wildfire smoke hazards in buildings, particularly schools.

Oct. 5, 2026: Message on Senate action sent to the House.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/5045
